one_month_reasoning: The window (last close Fri Oct 30, since Nov 1 is a Sunday) holds two dated events. (1) Q3-2026 results and Q4 guide, most likely Wed Oct 21 after the close (Nasdaq/Zacks 'expected'; TI's 2026 reports fell on Wednesdays; not yet confirmed by TI). Industry read-across still points to a beat on the $5.9B / $2.40 midpoint: ADI guided +7% q/q with price increases not yet in results, TI's July 1 price increases enforced on open POs, TPS/SN74 lead times extending (Fusion Greensheet Sep 2026). But the stock is +63% y/y and fell ~19% after a beat in July; TI's Q4 guide is usually seasonal-to-below, so the reaction is two-sided (+/-8-12% day plausible). (2) The $1.52 dividend goes ex on Oct 30 (record date Oct 30 under T+1), which mechanically lowers the Oct 30 close by ~$1.52 (~0.5%). I dropped the China anti-dumping ruling as an in-window catalyst: China committed on 2025-11-01 to terminate the probe and no MOFCOM ruling, extension or duty has been reported. Net: small positive earnings drift (~+0.5%) roughly offset by the ex-dividend drop, median ~$294, monthly sigma ~12.5% (42%/3.5, widened slightly for earnings).

comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: TXN trades at 29.9x CY27 on the same Zacks basis ($9.84) or 29.1x on LSEG $10.10, and ~19.9x CY27 EV/EBITDA: a ~30% premium to the 10-peer median and ~45% to the core median. I apply 24x P/E (+4% vs the 23.0x full median, +16% vs core, inside the range, below ADI 25.0x) and 16.5x EV/EBITDA (+15% vs 14.4x median, inside the range) to horizon NTM figures. Caveat: peers' Zacks panels may lag recent upward revisions as TXN's does, so the peer multiples may be a little high; applying them to the broader LSEG TXN EPS is slightly generous.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: A modest premium to the core median (~15%) is persistent through Oct-2027 for structural reasons with evidence: (a) highest gross margin in the set (61% in Q2-26, source 36/35) from owned 300mm analog capacity, which also lets TI supply and enforce price in a shortage while ADI quotes 60-70 wk lead times (source 20); (b) depreciation running above falling capex through 2028 plus $2.16B of CHIPS incentives to collect, so FCF exceeds net income; (c) Aa3/A+ balance sheet with pro-forma leverage only ~1x EBITDA after Silicon Labs. Against it: TXN's CY27 EPS growth (+16-19%) is the lowest in the core set, its cyclicality matches peers, and its multiple compressed late in the 2018 and 2022 upcycles - so no premium to ADI and nothing near today's ~30-45%. Sell-side outperform calls are not used.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$205 the market would be paying ~19x my haircut NTM EPS (~$10.8), under the 20.7x core peer median, or equivalently ~20x a CY28 EPS of ~$10: that means the upcycle has reversed into a double-ordering correction (lead times collapsing, distributor inventory rebuilding, price increases rolling back) or China's anti-dumping truce has broken down. It sits ~1.4 sigma-of-fundamentals below my base, beyond ordinary 42%-vol noise around a correct base case.

reasoning: Round 2 keeps my round-1 industry read and corrects the facts the supervisor established. Industry evidence is still strong for the next 2-3 quarters (ADI +40% y/y and guiding up, TI price increases enforced on open POs, TPS/SN74 lead times extending, ADI 60-70 wks), but these are textbook late-cycle markers; the 2010 (EE Times) and Q1-2018 (Morgan Stanley double-ordering survey, EMSNow) precedents put the analog revenue peak ~2 quarters after such signals, so I make an explicit call of ~55% that TI revenue peaks in Q1-Q3 2027, which justifies a ~5% expected haircut to the thin CY28 consensus. Corrections: Q2 EPS $2.14 GAAP (not $2.17); Silicon Labs now included on both sides of EV/EBITDA (net debt ~$9.0B at the horizon after retained FCF and part of the $2.16B CHIPS receivable, plus ~$0.35B SLAB EBITDA); China AD probe demoted from a dated catalyst to a truce-breakdown tail after the 2025-11-01 termination commitment (my search found no MOFCOM ruling); the horizon EPS is now a proper NTM blend (25% CY27 + 75% CY28) rather than all CY28; and peers are on one Nasdaq/Zacks CY27 basis (10 names, median 23.0x; core 20.7x). Fair value falls to $257 (24x x $10.78 = $259; 16.5x EBITDA = $253) from $269, mainly from the NTM blend and applying the cycle haircut to EBITDA too. Scenarios: bear $185 (22%), base $280 (53%), bull $385 (25%), mean ~$285; the price sits above fair value because the market is paying for the upcycle continuing, and I expect partial multiple compression rather than a full reversion within 12 months. Ladder: lognormal around a ~$283 median with sigma ~0.35, slightly fatter left tail than lognormal for a cycle reversal but thinner than round 1 because China duties are less likely and leverage is only ~1x. One-month ladder centered on ~$294 (small earnings drift offset by the $1.52 ex-dividend) with 12.5% sigma. Research limits: 6 searches/fetches this round; TI filings figures come via the supervisor's fact-check, not my own re-reading.
